title: add-ensemble-cohort-robustness-matrix-ci-hook
author: Priya Kothari
description:
Motivation: We see flurries of small, correlated drops across prompt cohorts after model rollouts. Individual cohort gates are noisy and can miss multivariate failure modes where several cohorts degrade slightly but together imply a material regression. This PR introduces a lightweight "robustness matrix" CI hook: an ensemble metric that combines cohort pass-rate delta, inter-cohort covariance, and calibration drift into a single score. The hook emits a per-prompt-set matrix and a scalar robustness index; the CI gate fails when the robustness index drops below configured thresholds or when correlated cohort failure mass exceeds a tunable fraction.

What this changes: Adds a new CI adapter (ci/hooks/robustness_matrix_hook.py) that: computes cohort-wise pass/fail deltas from the baseline, quantifies cross-cohort correlation using rank-based correlation on failure indicators, computes calibration drift over recent windows, and aggregates into a weighted robustness index. Adds an evaluator helper (eval/metrics/robustness_matrix.py) that provides the computation and a lightweight visualization helper for local debugging. Wire the hook into the eval-harness CI runner and the Linear-linked backfill job that can re-run historical cohorts to produce a baseline when the hook triggers.

Checklist: - [x] Metric definition and unit tests - [x] CI hook integration and smoke tests - [x] Backfill job stub and Linear link - [x] Docs: short docstring + README section - [x] Review feedback addressed

Backward compatibility and safety notes: The default gate is conservative (thresholds set to avoid false positives in canary churn). Config is feature-flagged per-repo and per-branch; it will only be enabled for select rollout lanes until we finish a 2-week trial. The hook logs granular signals for SRE and provides automatic fallback to ensemble-safe baseline when the hook is disabled.

Usage notes: The new gate exposes these override knobs via .ci-config/robustness_matrix.yaml: cohort_weighting, correlation_threshold, calibration_window_days, and fail_fraction. Example usage and recommended thresholds are documented in the README fragment.

Related: ENG-8472 (cohort cross-talk investigation), ENG-8521 (CI gating strategy).

review_comments: Elliot Ramos (2026-02-13): Can you clarify how the correlation is computed? Spearman or Pearson? Also add a short test that demonstrates a correlated two-cohort failure case.
Priya Kothari (2026-02-13): Reply: Using Spearman rank correlation to be robust to non-normal failure distributions; added unit test that simulates two cohorts with synchronized 6% drop.

Jin Park (2026-02-14): Suggestion: default correlation_threshold of 0.6 seems aggressive for small cohorts. Recommend 0.75 for large cohorts, 0.5 for micro cohorts; add adaptive thresholding to the README.
Priya Kothari (2026-02-15): Reply: Implemented adaptive thresholding based on cohort size; added parameter cohort_weighting and docs explaining recommended bins.
Aisha Thompson (2026-02-16): Request: please gate the backfill job behind a feature flag and ensure it uses the same evaluation seed for reproducibility.
Priya Kothari (2026-02-16): Reply: Backfill now checks .ci-config/feature_flags.yaml and uses a deterministic seed; added tests for determinism.
